notes.text: Kevin Bahl is out for the season and has missed the last 7 games. Joel Hanley has taken his spot beside Šimon Nemec. That pair has had 39% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 89:16 together, down from 46% with Bahl.
Martin Pospíšil has started killing penalties: on the ice for 31% of the team’s shorthanded time in 23 games, up from 2% last season.

Elmer Söderblom is out week to week (upper body injury) and has missed the last 9 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters. Rutger McGroarty has taken his spot beside Connor Dewar and Blake Lizotte.
Evgeni Malkin is out, reported after he played in their last game. He is a top-six forward.

Bryan Rust is on injured reserve (lower-body injury) and has missed the last 11 games. Tommy Novak has taken his spot beside Sidney Crosby and Rickard Rakell. That line has had 58% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 66:42 together, up from 43% with Rust.
Trevor van Riemsdyk returned in their last game after missing 15 games. Their recent numbers were built mostly without him.
Ilya Solovyov has started killing penalties: on the ice for 43% of the team’s shorthanded time in 3 games, up from 5% last season.
Nick Robertson has started killing penalties: on the ice for 30% of the team’s shorthanded time in 20 games, up from 2% with his old team last season.

PIT.head: Advantage, the Penguins
PIT.body: Pittsburgh has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage. The Flames can make it interesting if their penalty kill holds up.

CGY.head: The Flames face a real test
CGY.body: Pittsburgh has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage. The Flames can pull it off if their penalty kill holds up.

story.head: The Penguins are going to test Dustin Wolf early and often
paras: The Flames (10-12-1) lost 4-1 to Minnesota on Thursday, and the Penguins (7-12-2) lost 5-2 to St. Louis the same night. Going in, the Flames are sixth in the Pacific (tied for 23rd in the NHL) and the Pens last in the Metropolitan (tied for 28th).

The Flames’ record (.457) is about what their chances are worth. The Penguins have played better than their record (.381) says: their chances are worth about .538, and their finishing has held them back.

The Flames play some of the league’s fastest games (2nd) and have struggled on the power play (32nd). They also take a lot of low-quality shots (32nd), so the Penguins wait for good looks, but they settle for hopeful ones. Calgary has scored 2.48 goals a game, the third fewest in the league. As for the Penguins, they sit back rather than chase on the forecheck (lowest), get more of their shots from in close than anyone (1st) and rarely throw hits (lowest). The Penguins are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Flames.

Joel Farabee (7 G / 11 A / 18 P in 23 GP) leads the Flames in scoring, and Matt Coronato (5 G / 11 A / 16 P in 23 GP) isn’t far behind. For the Penguins, Erik Karlsson (3 G / 16 A / 19 P in 21 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Tommy Novak (8 G / 7 A / 15 P in 21 GP) has a team-high eight goals.
Dustin Wolf (5-6-1 / .877 SV% in 12 GS) will likely start for Calgary, and Sergei Murashov (2-5-1 / .893 SV% in 8 GS) for Pittsburgh.

At home, Dan Muse likes to send McGroarty, Lapierre and Koivunen out against opponents’ fourth lines, so watch for them against Tsyplakov, Castagna and Suniev. Elsewhere, the Penguins usually control more of the chances than the Flames do.
